items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: it struck me in listening to Cottrell's playing

ctx.x: No, I wouldn't think so because it's a different field. When you pick up the instrument and you feel it, you have a tendency to play it differently.
Well the reason I was thinking about that, because it struck me in listening to Cottrell's playing, that when he played tenor it was much like he'd play...
Well some of the things you do, yeah.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I think Cottrell made one or two arrangements.

ctx.x: Well, I'm trying to notice everything, you know. Well, that's great. You're inquisitive. You told me about how nothing was rehearsed yesterday. That amazed me because the band, you know, everything was so pretty. All the hominis seemed right to me, you know.

Right. Well, we rehearsed but not at the place. We rehearsed over the telephone. Oh. How did I do that? Yeah. Okay. I discussed it with Freddie Coleman. I told him, I said, you know what I want you to do, don't you? What? I said, well, I want you to do the same thing that you did last year. Bring that tambourine and watch my tempos. Well, I tell you to cut him and cut out and just listen to me. And he laughed. He says, okay. So, I did the same thing with Walter Lewis, but Walter had just recently played a concert…
So, you had no problem. It's just the guys worked together. Right. And they knew that I could play three-part harmony if you wanted them.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: In fact, Cottrell was my business manager all the way through.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. I guess that would attract people's attention and everything. That's right. Well, how often did you rehearse with that band?

Every time we could get a chance. You know, being a traveling band on the road and you stay up all night, you have to pick the times. And the times you were playing, maybe you had a couple of dates or you had a couple of days lay off. Well, I would call it a rehearsal and we'd rehearse that way. Or, if the guy, someone had heard an arrangement or a song they wanted to put an arrangement on, he would write it at intervals. And he'd let me know when it was ready. And, of course, I had Frank Jackie and Albert Martin…
Mm-hmm. What would be a business manager, then?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: He was one of the, he was an original member in my band.

ctx.x: He was one of the, he was an original member in my band.
I said, how long were you with the band? He said, oh, nine years. He gave the date, something like up to 1938 or something. I forget. That's right.
